## TL;DR

Completed the Control dashboard QA pass for task #1205. The substantive UI issue was the process table on narrow screens: its six columns were squeezed into the resource panel. The table now retains a readable minimum width inside its own horizontal scroller, so the page stays within the phone viewport while the table remains usable. Added deterministic preview data for populated resource captures and regression coverage for the component and responsive geometry. The requested QA record is in `docs/qa/2026-11-control-dashboard.md`.

## Work and rationale

I resumed this worktree after RepoOS reported that handoff stopped because the engineer-authored report draft did not exist. I first checked the task copy and current branch state, then read review pass 3 and the implementation diff. The latest review verdict is “good to go”; it reports no bugs or additional findings and says the desktop and 375px captures showed the intended contained scroller. `repoos landable 1205` also reported a clean worktree, clean merge with main, task-scoped paths, and the current review verdict, with the expected warning that a review lock is not present until handoff.

The implementation preserves the existing six-column grid but gives its header and rows a 560px minimum width. `.process-table-wrap` owns horizontal overflow, so at 375px the user can scroll the process columns without widening the dashboard itself. At desktop width the table fits in the wrapper. This is narrowly scoped to the resource panel's process table and avoids changing the layout of the surrounding cards.

The `system:processTable` shot fixture seeds stable machine, resource, repository, and process data, and pins it through the live sampler. In the component, the fixture also seeds enough history to show both sparklines promptly. This supports reproducible desktop and narrow captures and prevents the review image from depending on timing-sensitive live measurements. The fixture is registered centrally, and a component test checks that the representative process row and both sparklines actually render. The responsive test checks the CSS contract and, when bundled WebKit is installed, measures that the 375px table overflows only inside its wrapper while the 1280px table fits.

The QA document records the requested real, empty, and service-error states at 1280×1200 and 375×1200, along with the headless auth-less server method and capture filenames. The task's two screenshot declarations target the resource panel and process-table wrapper at the two required viewport widths.

## Approaches tried

The review trail shows the work was iterated through multiple passes before this resume. An earlier pass raised a formatting failure, which was corrected before the later “good to go” review. During the prior validation work, a component assertion expected the header as uppercase `RUNTIME` even though the component preserves the title-case text `Runtime`; that assertion was adjusted to be case-insensitive. The final regression assertion remains tolerant of presentation casing while still verifying the expected header is present.

For the narrow table, retaining a compressed six-column grid would make labels and values difficult to scan. The chosen approach keeps a minimum readable table width and puts scrolling on its immediate wrapper. For captures, waiting on the live resource sampler would make screenshots nondeterministic; the explicit fixture keeps the underlying panel behavior intact while making the state stable for preview capture.

## Challenges and blockers

The only blocker in the current handoff attempt was procedural: RepoOS could not finalize the engineering report because the required draft file was missing. This session supplies it. The branch itself is clean, and the latest review and landability check show no outstanding implementation findings. The required `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed on this worktree, including remote changed-path tests, rendered contrast, and UI smoke.

## Key learnings

Responsive tables should preserve the column geometry that makes their data legible, while constraining overflow to the smallest sensible container. Preview fixtures are most useful when they seed the same component data path that real data uses and are pinned against asynchronous refreshes. Finally, assertions for user-facing labels should verify semantic presence without making tests depend on incidental capitalization when case is not part of the contract.
